subject: Chemistry
title: Structure of Atom
description: This chapter explores the evolution of atomic models, subatomic particles, electromagnetic radiation, quantum theory, atomic spectra, Bohr's model, quantum mechanical model, and electronic configuration.
learning_objectives: Understand the discovery of subatomic particles.
Study electromagnetic radiation and atomic spectra.
Understand quantum theory and wave-particle duality.
Learn quantum numbers and their significance.
Write electronic configurations of atoms and ions.
key_points: Atoms consist of electrons, protons and neutrons.
J.J. Thomson proposed the Plum Pudding Model.
Rutherford discovered the atomic nucleus through alpha scattering experiments.
Bohr explained the hydrogen spectrum using quantized energy levels.
Matter exhibits both particle and wave nature.
Heisenberg's Uncertainty Principle limits simultaneous measurement of position and momentum.
Quantum numbers describe the location and behavior of electrons.
Electronic configuration follows Aufbau Principle, Pauli Exclusion Principle and Hund's Rule.

important_laws.name: Planck's Quantum Theory
important_laws.statement: Energy is emitted or absorbed in discrete packets called quanta.

important_laws.name: Heisenberg's Uncertainty Principle
important_laws.statement: Position and momentum of a particle cannot both be measured accurately at the same time.

important_laws.name: Pauli Exclusion Principle
important_laws.statement: No two electrons in an atom can have the same set of four quantum numbers.

important_laws.name: Hund's Rule
important_laws.statement: Electrons occupy degenerate orbitals singly before pairing.

notes: Atoms are composed of subatomic particles.
Bohr's model successfully explained hydrogen spectrum.
Quantum mechanics replaced classical atomic models.
Electrons occupy atomic orbitals instead of fixed paths.
